clue.text: Vehicle insurance required to cross upper-class Canadian city

parts.note: a van is a goods vehicle

indicators.note: one piece crossing another lies across it, so the insurance word straddles the upper-class letter

parts.note: cover is insurance protection

explanation.surface: A driver discovers that motor insurance must stretch to a posh trip across a Canadian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major port city in British Columbia, Canada.

clue.text: There's this malice in missive, no mistake

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: Someone detects unmistakable spite in a letter they have received.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'missiVE NO Mistake'; 'There's this' just leads in.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom in its figurative sense is bitter spite or ill will.

clue.text: Silver's following Tonto's third horse

indicators.note: silver comes after the letter taken from Tonto, so it is placed second
the third letter of the sidekick's name is taken

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: The Lone Ranger's horse Silver trots behind Tonto's mount.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver and Tonto are the Lone Ranger's horse and companion, but here Silver is just the chemical symbol AG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old or worn-out horse.

clue.text: In a difficult situation there

definitions.meaning: put in an awkward position, pressed for an answer
present at the very place, in situ

explanation.surface: A double definition reading as a note about being stuck in a tricky spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both being put under pressure and being physically present at the scene.

clue.text: Tourist, Italian, wearing eyeshade

indicators.note: the eyeshade is worn over the Italian, so it goes around those letters

parts.note: a visor is a peak shading the eyes

explanation.surface: A sightseer from Italy sports a sun visor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a visitor to a place on holiday.

clue.text: Love affair beginning in remote country church

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A love affair starts in a little church in a far-flung country.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, especially a passionate one.

clue.text: Note no intro for stringed instrument

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter, its introduction

parts.note: a sharp is a note raised a semitone

explanation.surface: A musical observation that a stringed instrument starts without an introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: The harp is a large plucked instrument with many strings.

clue.text: Row after vehicle on round brings contaminant

indicators.note: in a down answer the vehicle sits on top of the round letter
the row word follows the other two pieces

parts.note: a vehicle in the sense of a means or medium is an agent
O is round in shape
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: A quarrel after a car runs over something brings pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a line, RANGE; 'vehicle' is a means of conveying something, AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent Orange was a toxic herbicide and defoliant used in the Vietnam War, notorious for its dioxin.

clue.text: Page handed over is liked better

parts.note: referred, as a matter passed to someone else

explanation.surface: A page that has been passed on is the one somebody favours.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferred means favoured over the alternatives.

clue.text: See 22
Man on board losing head in the dark

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece, a man on the board

explanation.surface: A sailor is lost overboard, head first, in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a ship but means a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness between dusk and dawn.

clue.text: Homes were vandalised, at a place not specified

indicators.note: smashed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report that houses were wrecked at an undisclosed location.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in or at some unnamed location.

clue.text: Changed them at one, shabby in appearance

indicators.note: altered, so the letters of the next three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clothes swapped all at once still look scruffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally eaten by moths, the word figuratively means worn-out and tatty.

clue.text: Newspaper article on grown-up children

parts.note: the definite article
big means adult or grown
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature about adult offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Issue is a British street magazine sold by homeless vendors.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is a periodical publication, loosely called a newspaper here.

clue.text: Fool about to produce gunpowder ingredient

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a nitwit
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: An idiot is about to make gunpowder, with predictable results.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is the oxidising component of black powder.

clue.text: Soccer player in rear of bus with someone crying

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a weeper is one who weeps

explanation.surface: A footballer sits at the back of the team coach in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeper is a defender who plays behind the back line in football.

clue.text: Flavour of small juicy fruit, perfect

parts.note: a pear is a juicy fruit
mint means in perfect condition

explanation.surface: A taste described as like a small, perfect juicy fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a mint plant used as a common flavouring, as in chewing gum.

clue.text: Sovereign exercises right in capital, upon return

indicators.note: the exercise and right letters go inside the turned capital
the capital's name is read backwards

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: A monarch claims his privilege in the capital on coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' is physical education, the school subject, not a verb; 'upon return' turns only the capital, giving EMOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme sovereign ruler of an empire.

clue.text: Preparation for eyesight

parts.note: pro means in favour of
vision is the power of sight

explanation.surface: Something done to get ready for an eye test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but supplies PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Provision is preparation made in advance for future needs.

clue.text: Was left holding son

indicators.note: the leaving word contains the son's letter

parts.note: exited means went out, left

explanation.surface: Someone departed carrying a baby boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is a verb in the past tense, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Existed means had being, a past tense like the verb of being in the clue.

clue.text: See cod? I see flounders

indicators.note: struggles clumsily, so the letters stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A fish-spotter notices a cod and some flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounders' looks like more fish but is a verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's seat or jurisdiction, the area governed being the diocese.

clue.text: Boasted about any number installed

indicators.note: the boasting word goes around the number letter

parts.note: crowed means bragged
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: Someone bragged about the number of devices put in.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is installed on the throne at a coronation, so crowned fits.

clue.text: Cold and stern — welcoming to architect?

indicators.note: the rear takes in the little word, so it goes inside

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a boat

explanation.surface: A chilly, severe person giving a frosty welcome to a building designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like an adjective but is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect in the wider sense is the maker or originator of something; the query flags the stretch.

clue.text: Rule: keep leader of government in check

indicators.note: the check word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A political maxim: always keep the head of government in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Reign means the period or act of ruling as monarch.

clue.text: Sound of a bell heard by Welsh boy and English actress

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, its silent first letter vanishing

parts.note: a knell is the tolling of a bell
Gwyn is a Welsh male name

explanation.surface: A Welsh lad and an English actress hear a bell toll.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell Gwyn was a Restoration actress and mistress of Charles II.

clue.text: Wisecracks made by individuals touring ship

indicators.note: the individuals go round the ship, enclosing it

parts.note: ones are single individuals
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: Passengers on a cruise trade witty remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: One-liners are short jokes or quips delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Delay eating a Malaysian dish

indicators.note: the delay word swallows the letter

parts.note: to stay is to postpone or delay

explanation.surface: A hold-up while someone eats a meal from Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is grilled skewered meat with peanut sauce, from Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Rude when drinking drop of vodka on the rocks

indicators.note: the rude word takes in the letter

parts.note: insolent means rude

indicators.note: just a drop, the first letter, of the word

explanation.surface: A rude drinker downing vodka over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' suggests a drink with ice but means bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is failing or bankrupt, unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: Small figure in corner may be from fashionable collection

parts.note: in means in fashion
a set is a collection

explanation.surface: A tiny illustration in the corner may come from a trendy range.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture or map set within a larger one, often in a corner.

clue.text: Blubber may be extracted from whales, obviously

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Fat clearly comes from whales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' looks like whale fat but is the verb to cry; the letters run across 'whaleS OBviously'.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to weep noisily, to sob.

clue.text: Row in dead heat on river

parts.note: a tie is a dead heat

explanation.surface: A rowing race ends in a dead heat on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests rowing but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row, especially one of several rising rows of seats.

clue.text: One delivering goods, perhaps confused by an order

indicators.note: mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A delivery worker bewildered by an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand boy is a lad who runs errands such as delivering shopping, so 'perhaps' marks an example.
